text.p: Aluminium producer Capral Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday it agreed with the general expectation that reasonable industry balance would underpin current aluminium price levels.

"The opening up of the global aluminium industry, especially to metal supply from the former CIS states, does now seem to be a stabilising force reducing the likelihood of a 1989-type metal shortage and price spike," Capral chairman Jeremy Davis told the company's annual meeting.
However, price pressure in times of excess capacity was likely to come from the increasing fragmentation of smelter ownership.
The lack of any renewed Memorandum of Understanding in future industry cycles could mean a cap on upside movements but an unlimited downside, Capral said.
The previous Memorandum of Understanding between aluminium producing countries required producers to limit output until price levels recovered.
By 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT), Capral shares were one cent higher at A$4.22 on turnover of 1.03 million shares.
